title: The kinds of value
objective: Recognise whole numbers, decimals, text, true and false, and nothing, and write each one as a literal.

body.text: A value written directly in the code is a literal. Lagom has a few kinds of literal. A whole number is written without a point, such as 42. A decimal has a point, such as 3.5. Text is written inside double quotes, such as "hello". true and false are the two truth values. nothing means no value at all.

body.title: Each kind of literal
body.code:
make whole equal to 42
make precise equal to 3.5
make greeting equal to "hello"
make enabled equal to true
make missing equal to nothing
say whole
say precise
say greeting
say enabled
say missing

body.text: Quotes make the difference between text and a name. say "score" prints the word score. say score prints the value held in the variable called score. Text in quotes is never looked up as a name.

body.title: Text is not a name
body.code:
make score equal to 10
say "score"
say score

body.prompt: Make answer hold the whole number 42, not the text "42". Then say it. The program should print 42.
body.starter:
make answer equal to "42"
say answer
body.solution:
make answer equal to 42
say answer

checks.description: answer is set to the number 42, with no quotes
